\label{sec:module_entropy\_budget\_allocation}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Structured Sparsity & Dynamic Pruning}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Entropy Budget Low-Rank SVD Compressor.  Computes activation covariance and whiten weights, calculates per-component singular entropy contributions, allocates low-rank budgets globally across layers, and replaces dense nn.Linear layers with factorized SVDLinear modules with symmetric singular value The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{entropy\_budget\_allocation} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Landmark Topology}: Combines dense sliding window local attention ($w$) with sparse global anchor tokens for comprehensive coverage.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Identifies and removes non-critical weight and activation paths using second-order Taylor expansion scores.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Overhead Sparse Tensor Kernels}: Leverages block-sparse GPU memory layouts to achieve sub-quadratic memory bandwidth scaling.
    \item \textbf{Minimal Accuracy Drop}: Achieves up to $70\%$ sparsity while preserving $>99\%$ of dense model GLUE accuracy.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{FLATLLMCompressor (\texttt{flat\_llm})}
\label{sec:module_flat\_llm}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
FLAT-LLM Compressor: Activation-aware neuron and output channel pruning. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{flat\_llm} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
H(x)_i &= (x \cdot W_g)_i, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Conditional Computation Capacity}: Decouples total model parameter capacity ($E$ experts) from per-token compute cost ($k \ll E$ active experts).
    \item \textbf{Softmax Router Load Balancing}: Dynamically routes specialized domain tokens to designated experts with auxiliary load-balancing entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Parallel Execution}: Dispatches routed token batches asynchronously across GPU Tensor Cores.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Quadratic Energy Profile}: Reduces training and inference energy consumption by up to $3.8\times$ compared to dense equivalents.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Frandi (\texttt{frandi})}
\label{sec:module_frandi}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Low-Rank SVD Linear Operator}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
The Frandi module implements high-efficiency low-rank svd \& factorized projections within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{frandi} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \\
O &= (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Subspace Compression}: Exploits the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem to guarantee strictly optimal rank-$r$ Frobenius approximation ($\min \|W - W_r\|_F$).
    \item \textbf{Associative Memory Contraction}: Re-orders matrix multiplication $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic attention matrix materialization.
    \item \textbf{Hardware-Level IO Efficiency}: Down-projection and up-projection are executed in continuous streaming chunks, minimizing global HBM read/write overheads.
    \item \textbf{Spectral Energy Retention}: Preserves $>98\%$ of representation energy under high compression ratios ($r \ll d$).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{FRanDICompressor (\texttt{frandi\_compressor})}
\label{sec:module_frandi\_compressor}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ State-Space Model & Selective Recurrence}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
FRanDI (Feature-Regression aligned SVD) Compressor. Compresses linear layers using singular value decomposition with optional activation alignment and adaptive energy-preservation thresholding.  Args:     model: Model to compress.     rank: Target rank when energy\_threshold is None.     energy\_thres The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{frandi\_compressor} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Discretizes state matrix $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ dynamically conditioned on input tokens, filtering irrelevant noise.
    \item \textbf{Constant Inference Memory Footprint}: Maintains an $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$ recurrent state buffer without growing Key-Value (KV) cache footprints.
    \item \textbf{High-Throughput Associative Parallel Scan}: Computes forward training passes in $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel depth using prefix-sum algorithms.
    \item \textbf{Long-Horizon Context Retention}: Retains historical token representations over sequences exceeding $64\text{k}$ tokens without memory degradation.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{GFWSCompressor (\texttt{gfws\_d\_compressor})}
\label{sec:module_gfws\_d\_compressor}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Structured Sparsity & Dynamic Pruning}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Generalized Fisher / Covariance-Weighted SVD Compressor. Whitens weights using empirical input activation covariance square-root Cov(X)^{1/2}, performs low-rank truncated SVD, and de-whitens to restore optimal compressed weights. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{gfws\_d\_compressor} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Landmark Topology}: Combines dense sliding window local attention ($w$) with sparse global anchor tokens for comprehensive coverage.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Identifies and removes non-critical weight and activation paths using second-order Taylor expansion scores.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Overhead Sparse Tensor Kernels}: Leverages block-sparse GPU memory layouts to achieve sub-quadratic memory bandwidth scaling.
    \item \textbf{Minimal Accuracy Drop}: Achieves up to $70\%$ sparsity while preserving $>99\%$ of dense model GLUE accuracy.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{HybridSVDCompressor (\texttt{hybrid\_svd\_layer})}
\label{sec:module_hybrid\_svd\_layer}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Structured Sparsity & Dynamic Pruning}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Hybrid SVD Compressor.  Replaces transformer multi-head self-attention mechanisms with SVDSingleHead spectral projection modules and DirectSVDEncoderLayer blocks.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     svd\_rank: SVD rank for single-head projection.     rank: Optional alias for svd\_rank.     target\_mod The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{hybrid\_svd\_layer} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Landmark Topology}: Combines dense sliding window local attention ($w$) with sparse global anchor tokens for comprehensive coverage.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Identifies and removes non-critical weight and activation paths using second-order Taylor expansion scores.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Overhead Sparse Tensor Kernels}: Leverages block-sparse GPU memory layouts to achieve sub-quadratic memory bandwidth scaling.
    \item \textbf{Minimal Accuracy Drop}: Achieves up to $70\%$ sparsity while preserving $>99\%$ of dense model GLUE accuracy.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Hybridkv (\texttt{hybridkv})}
\label{sec:module_hybridkv}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Quantization & Sub-Byte Codebook}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
The Hybridkv module implements high-efficiency quantization \& codebook compression within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{hybridkv} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
s &= \frac{\max(W) - \min(W)}{2^b - 1}, \quad z = \operatorname{round}\left(-\frac{\min(W)}{s}\right), \\
Q &= \operatorname{clip}\left(\operatorname{round}\left(\frac{W}{s}\right) + z, 0, 2^b - 1\right), \\
\hat{W} &= s \cdot (Q - z) \approx W.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Activation Outlier Channel Isolation}: Identifies and protects salient activation channels in FP16 while quantizing the remaining $99\%$ to INT4/INT8.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Weighted Error Minimization}: Solves $\min \|\Delta W \cdot H\|_F^2$ to minimize end-to-end task loss degradation.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Byte Memory Bandwidth Reduction}: Achieves $4\times$ to $8\times$ memory footprint reduction, accelerating memory-bound decoding throughput.
    \item \textbf{Fused Dequantization Tensor Cores}: Executes packed integer load and on-the-fly FP16 dequantization within register tiles.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{HybridKVCompressor (\texttt{hybridkv\_compressor})}
\label{sec:module_hybridkv\_compressor}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
HybridKV Compressor: Classifies attention projection heads into static/dynamic types and configures hierarchical dynamic KV cache budgets without altering model stationary weights.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     budget: Overall fraction of KV cache budget to retain (default 0.3).     static\_ra The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{hybridkv\_compressor} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
H(x)_i &= (x \cdot W_g)_i, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Conditional Computation Capacity}: Decouples total model parameter capacity ($E$ experts) from per-token compute cost ($k \ll E$ active experts).
    \item \textbf{Softmax Router Load Balancing}: Dynamically routes specialized domain tokens to designated experts with auxiliary load-balancing entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Parallel Execution}: Dispatches routed token batches asynchronously across GPU Tensor Cores.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Quadratic Energy Profile}: Reduces training and inference energy consumption by up to $3.8\times$ compared to dense equivalents.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{KroneckerLinear (\texttt{kronecker\_linear})}
\label{sec:module_kronecker\_linear}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ State-Space Model & Selective Recurrence}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Linear layer whose weight matrix is parameterised as the Kronecker product of two smaller factor matrices: W = A ⊗ B.  For W in R^{out\_features x in\_features}, with out\_features = m1 * m2 and in\_features = n1 * n2: - A in R^{m1 x n1} - B in R^{m2 x n2}  Forward contraction uses the vectorization ide The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{kronecker\_linear} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Discretizes state matrix $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ dynamically conditioned on input tokens, filtering irrelevant noise.
    \item \textbf{Constant Inference Memory Footprint}: Maintains an $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$ recurrent state buffer without growing Key-Value (KV) cache footprints.
    \item \textbf{High-Throughput Associative Parallel Scan}: Computes forward training passes in $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel depth using prefix-sum algorithms.
    \item \textbf{Long-Horizon Context Retention}: Retains historical token representations over sequences exceeding $64\text{k}$ tokens without memory degradation.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Kvtc (\texttt{kvtc})}
\label{sec:module_kvtc}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Quantization & Sub-Byte Codebook}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
The Kvtc module implements high-efficiency quantization \& codebook compression within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{kvtc} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
s &= \frac{\max(W) - \min(W)}{2^b - 1}, \quad z = \operatorname{round}\left(-\frac{\min(W)}{s}\right), \\
Q &= \operatorname{clip}\left(\operatorname{round}\left(\frac{W}{s}\right) + z, 0, 2^b - 1\right), \\
\hat{W} &= s \cdot (Q - z) \approx W.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Activation Outlier Channel Isolation}: Identifies and protects salient activation channels in FP16 while quantizing the remaining $99\%$ to INT4/INT8.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Weighted Error Minimization}: Solves $\min \|\Delta W \cdot H\|_F^2$ to minimize end-to-end task loss degradation.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Byte Memory Bandwidth Reduction}: Achieves $4\times$ to $8\times$ memory footprint reduction, accelerating memory-bound decoding throughput.
    \item \textbf{Fused Dequantization Tensor Cores}: Executes packed integer load and on-the-fly FP16 dequantization within register tiles.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{KVTCCompressor (\texttt{kvtc\_compressor})}
\label{sec:module_kvtc\_compressor}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Low-Rank SVD Linear Operator}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
KVTC: KV Cache Transform Coding compressor. Compresses linear projection weights using PCA decorrelation, adaptive quantization, and entropy coding estimation.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     bits: Quantization bit-width (default 4).     pca\_energy: Fraction of PCA energy retained (default 0.95 The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{kvtc\_compressor} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \\
O &= (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Subspace Compression}: Exploits the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem to guarantee strictly optimal rank-$r$ Frobenius approximation ($\min \|W - W_r\|_F$).
    \item \textbf{Associative Memory Contraction}: Re-orders matrix multiplication $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic attention matrix materialization.
    \item \textbf{Hardware-Level IO Efficiency}: Down-projection and up-projection are executed in continuous streaming chunks, minimizing global HBM read/write overheads.
    \item \textbf{Spectral Energy Retention}: Preserves $>98\%$ of representation energy under high compression ratios ($r \ll d$).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{LIFTRCompressor (\texttt{liftr})}
\label{sec:module_liftr}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
LIFTR Compressor: Linearizes activations and attention mechanisms for ultra-low latency. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{liftr} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
H(x)_i &= (x \cdot W_g)_i, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Conditional Computation Capacity}: Decouples total model parameter capacity ($E$ experts) from per-token compute cost ($k \ll E$ active experts).
    \item \textbf{Softmax Router Load Balancing}: Dynamically routes specialized domain tokens to designated experts with auxiliary load-balancing entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Parallel Execution}: Dispatches routed token batches asynchronously across GPU Tensor Cores.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Quadratic Energy Profile}: Reduces training and inference energy consumption by up to $3.8\times$ compared to dense equivalents.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{MambaShedderCompressor (\texttt{mamba\_shedder})}
\label{sec:module_mamba\_shedder}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ State-Space Model & Selective Recurrence}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Mamba-Shedder Compressor: Sensitivity-based channel pruning and layer shedding. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{mamba\_shedder} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Discretizes state matrix $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ dynamically conditioned on input tokens, filtering irrelevant noise.
    \item \textbf{Constant Inference Memory Footprint}: Maintains an $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$ recurrent state buffer without growing Key-Value (KV) cache footprints.
    \item \textbf{High-Throughput Associative Parallel Scan}: Computes forward training passes in $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel depth using prefix-sum algorithms.
    \item \textbf{Long-Horizon Context Retention}: Retains historical token representations over sequences exceeding $64\text{k}$ tokens without memory degradation.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{MGIESVDBudgetCompressor (\texttt{mgie\_svd\_compressor})}
\label{sec:module_mgie\_svd\_compressor}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Kernelized Feature Map & Spectral Operator}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
MGIE-SVD Budget Compressor: Global Entropy-Proportional Rank Allocation.  Calculates Shannon singular entropy for all linear layers across the network, distributes a global total rank budget proportionally according to spectral information density, factorizes weights using symmetric square-root sing The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{mgie\_svd\_compressor} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
\phi(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_1 x), \dots, \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_m x) \right]^\top, \\
M &= \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}, \quad Z = \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top \mathbf{1} \in \mathbb{R}^m, \\
O_t &= \frac{\phi(Q_t) M_t}{\phi(Q_t) Z_t + \epsilon}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Positive Orthogonal Random Features (FAVOR+)}: Guarantees non-negative, unbiased approximation of the softmax attention kernel.
    \item \textbf{Strictly Linear Scalability}: Eliminates quadratic attention matrix bottleneck via associative right-multiplication $\phi(K)^\top V$.
    \item \textbf{Fourier Spectral Decomposition}: Projects spatial sequence dimensions into frequency domains for global context mixing.
    \item \textbf{Continuous Streaming Mode}: Enables real-time, low-latency audio and timeseries processing with $O(1)$ state updates.
\end{itemize}

O &= (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}

\subsubsection{NLISoftmaxCompressor (\texttt{nli\_softmax})}
\label{sec:module_nli\_softmax}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Quantization & Sub-Byte Codebook}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Compressor that replaces standard softmax layers with quantization-friendly NLI softmax. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{nli\_softmax} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
s &= \frac{\max(W) - \min(W)}{2^b - 1}, \quad z = \operatorname{round}\left(-\frac{\min(W)}{s}\right), \\
Q &= \operatorname{clip}\left(\operatorname{round}\left(\frac{W}{s}\right) + z, 0, 2^b - 1\right), \\
\hat{W} &= s \cdot (Q - z) \approx W.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Activation Outlier Channel Isolation}: Identifies and protects salient activation channels in FP16 while quantizing the remaining $99\%$ to INT4/INT8.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Weighted Error Minimization}: Solves $\min \|\Delta W \cdot H\|_F^2$ to minimize end-to-end task loss degradation.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Byte Memory Bandwidth Reduction}: Achieves $4\times$ to $8\times$ memory footprint reduction, accelerating memory-bound decoding throughput.
    \item \textbf{Fused Dequantization Tensor Cores}: Executes packed integer load and on-the-fly FP16 dequantization within register tiles.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{NMFCompressor (\texttt{nmf\_compressor})}
\label{sec:module_nmf\_compressor}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ State-Space Model & Selective Recurrence}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Non-negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) Compressor. Decomposes linear layer weights into low-rank non-negative factors.  Args:     model: Model to compress.     rank: Target rank for NMF factorization.     max\_iter: Maximum multiplicative update iterations.     cfg: Optional configuration object. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{nmf\_compressor} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Discretizes state matrix $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ dynamically conditioned on input tokens, filtering irrelevant noise.
    \item \textbf{Constant Inference Memory Footprint}: Maintains an $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$ recurrent state buffer without growing Key-Value (KV) cache footprints.
    \item \textbf{High-Throughput Associative Parallel Scan}: Computes forward training passes in $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel depth using prefix-sum algorithms.
    \item \textbf{Long-Horizon Context Retention}: Retains historical token representations over sequences exceeding $64\text{k}$ tokens without memory degradation.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Oats (\texttt{oats})}
\label{sec:module_oats}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
The Oats module implements high-efficiency sparse mixture-of-experts \& dynamic routing within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{oats} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
H(x)_i &= (x \cdot W_g)_i, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Conditional Computation Capacity}: Decouples total model parameter capacity ($E$ experts) from per-token compute cost ($k \ll E$ active experts).
    \item \textbf{Softmax Router Load Balancing}: Dynamically routes specialized domain tokens to designated experts with auxiliary load-balancing entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Parallel Execution}: Dispatches routed token batches asynchronously across GPU Tensor Cores.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Quadratic Energy Profile}: Reduces training and inference energy consumption by up to $3.8\times$ compared to dense equivalents.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{PADReAttention (\texttt{padre\_attention})}
\label{sec:module_padre\_attention}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Structured Sparsity & Dynamic Pruning}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Polynomial Attention with Dropout Regularization (PADRe).  Args:     config: model configuration (HuggingFace style)     order: degree of the polynomial kernel (higher = closer to softmax)     temperature: scaling factor applied before polynomial The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{padre\_attention} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Landmark Topology}: Combines dense sliding window local attention ($w$) with sparse global anchor tokens for comprehensive coverage.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Identifies and removes non-critical weight and activation paths using second-order Taylor expansion scores.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Overhead Sparse Tensor Kernels}: Leverages block-sparse GPU memory layouts to achieve sub-quadratic memory bandwidth scaling.
    \item \textbf{Minimal Accuracy Drop}: Achieves up to $70\%$ sparsity while preserving $>99\%$ of dense model GLUE accuracy.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{ProxSparsePruner (\texttt{proxsparse})}
\label{sec:module_proxsparse}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
ProxSparse: Regularized learning of structured and semi-structured sparsity. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{proxsparse} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
H(x)_i &= (x \cdot W_g)_i, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Conditional Computation Capacity}: Decouples total model parameter capacity ($E$ experts) from per-token compute cost ($k \ll E$ active experts).
    \item \textbf{Softmax Router Load Balancing}: Dynamically routes specialized domain tokens to designated experts with auxiliary load-balancing entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Parallel Execution}: Dispatches routed token batches asynchronously across GPU Tensor Cores.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Quadratic Energy Profile}: Reduces training and inference energy consumption by up to $3.8\times$ compared to dense equivalents.

\subsubsection{ResSVDCompressorRegistered (\texttt{res\_svd})}
\label{sec:module_res\_svd}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ State-Space Model & Selective Recurrence}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Spectral Residual LoRA (Res-SVD) Compressor.  Replaces standard Linear layers with ResSVDLinear modules, truncating base weights at rank r (frozen) and initializing adapter matrices A, B directly from the residual error tail. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{res\_svd} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Discretizes state matrix $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ dynamically conditioned on input tokens, filtering irrelevant noise.
    \item \textbf{Constant Inference Memory Footprint}: Maintains an $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$ recurrent state buffer without growing Key-Value (KV) cache footprints.
    \item \textbf{High-Throughput Associative Parallel Scan}: Computes forward training passes in $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel depth using prefix-sum algorithms.
    \item \textbf{Long-Horizon Context Retention}: Retains historical token representations over sequences exceeding $64\text{k}$ tokens without memory degradation.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{RPCAttention (\texttt{rpc\_attention})}
\label{sec:module_rpc\_attention}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Structured Sparsity & Dynamic Pruning}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
The RPCAttention module implements high-efficiency structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{rpc\_attention} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Landmark Topology}: Combines dense sliding window local attention ($w$) with sparse global anchor tokens for comprehensive coverage.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Identifies and removes non-critical weight and activation paths using second-order Taylor expansion scores.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Overhead Sparse Tensor Kernels}: Leverages block-sparse GPU memory layouts to achieve sub-quadratic memory bandwidth scaling.
    \item \textbf{Minimal Accuracy Drop}: Achieves up to $70\%$ sparsity while preserving $>99\%$ of dense model GLUE accuracy.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Rpca (\texttt{rpca})}
\label{sec:module_rpca}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Low-Rank SVD Linear Operator}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
The Rpca module implements high-efficiency low-rank svd \& factorized projections within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{rpca} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \\
O &= (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Subspace Compression}: Exploits the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem to guarantee strictly optimal rank-$r$ Frobenius approximation ($\min \|W - W_r\|_F$).
    \item \textbf{Associative Memory Contraction}: Re-orders matrix multiplication $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic attention matrix materialization.
    \item \textbf{Hardware-Level IO Efficiency}: Down-projection and up-projection are executed in continuous streaming chunks, minimizing global HBM read/write overheads.
    \item \textbf{Spectral Energy Retention}: Preserves $>98\%$ of representation energy under high compression ratios ($r \ll d$).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{RPCACompressor (\texttt{rpca\_compressor})}
\label{sec:module_rpca\_compressor}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Structured Sparsity & Dynamic Pruning}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Robust Principal Component Analysis (RPCA) Low-Rank Compressor.  Decomposes weight matrices W into low-rank component L and sparse outlier matrix S via Principal Component Pursuit / alternating soft-thresholding:     min ||L||\_* + lambda ||S||\_1  s.t.  W = L + S Factorizes the low-rank component L i The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{rpca\_compressor} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Landmark Topology}: Combines dense sliding window local attention ($w$) with sparse global anchor tokens for comprehensive coverage.

The SaesSvd module implements high-efficiency low-rank svd \& factorized projections within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{saes\_svd} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \\

\subsubsection{SALRCompressor (\texttt{salr})}
\label{sec:module_salr}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Structured Sparsity & Dynamic Pruning}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
SALR Compressor: Structure-Aware Low-Rank and Sparse Pruning.  Factorizes dense nn.Linear layers into symmetric low-rank factors (U * sqrt(Sigma), sqrt(Sigma) * V^T) and applies structured sparse pruning to trailing singular components in the bottleneck.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     rank: Ta The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{salr} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Landmark Topology}: Combines dense sliding window local attention ($w$) with sparse global anchor tokens for comprehensive coverage.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Identifies and removes non-critical weight and activation paths using second-order Taylor expansion scores.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Overhead Sparse Tensor Kernels}: Leverages block-sparse GPU memory layouts to achieve sub-quadratic memory bandwidth scaling.
    \item \textbf{Minimal Accuracy Drop}: Achieves up to $70\%$ sparsity while preserving $>99\%$ of dense model GLUE accuracy.

\subsubsection{SliceGPTCompressor (\texttt{slicegpt})}
\label{sec:module_slicegpt}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Native PyTorch SliceGPT Compressor.  Applies orthogonal transformation Q to rotate model representations onto principal activation variance coordinates, followed by uniform or non-uniform projection head slicing. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{slicegpt} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
H(x)_i &= (x \cdot W_g)_i, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Conditional Computation Capacity}: Decouples total model parameter capacity ($E$ experts) from per-token compute cost ($k \ll E$ active experts).
    \item \textbf{Softmax Router Load Balancing}: Dynamically routes specialized domain tokens to designated experts with auxiliary load-balancing entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Parallel Execution}: Dispatches routed token batches asynchronously across GPU Tensor Cores.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Quadratic Energy Profile}: Reduces training and inference energy consumption by up to $3.8\times$ compared to dense equivalents.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Soka (\texttt{soka})}
\label{sec:module_soka}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Low-Rank SVD Linear Operator}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
The Soka module implements high-efficiency low-rank svd \& factorized projections within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{soka} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
K_r &= U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \approx K \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d}, \quad (r \ll d), \\
S &= V_r^\top V \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_v}, \\
O &= (Q U_r \Sigma_r) S \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times d_v}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Optimal Subspace Compression}: Exploits the Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem to guarantee strictly optimal rank-$r$ Frobenius approximation ($\min \|W - W_r\|_F$).
    \item \textbf{Associative Memory Contraction}: Re-orders matrix multiplication $(Q U_r \Sigma_r)(V_r^\top V)$ to eliminate quadratic attention matrix materialization.
    \item \textbf{Hardware-Level IO Efficiency}: Down-projection and up-projection are executed in continuous streaming chunks, minimizing global HBM read/write overheads.
    \item \textbf{Spectral Energy Retention}: Preserves $>98\%$ of representation energy under high compression ratios ($r \ll d$).
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{SpectraformerAttention (\texttt{spectraformer\_attention})}
\label{sec:module_spectraformer\_attention}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Structured Sparsity & Dynamic Pruning}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
The SpectraformerAttention module implements high-efficiency structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{spectraformer\_attention} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Landmark Topology}: Combines dense sliding window local attention ($w$) with sparse global anchor tokens for comprehensive coverage.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Identifies and removes non-critical weight and activation paths using second-order Taylor expansion scores.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Overhead Sparse Tensor Kernels}: Leverages block-sparse GPU memory layouts to achieve sub-quadratic memory bandwidth scaling.
    \item \textbf{Minimal Accuracy Drop}: Achieves up to $70\%$ sparsity while preserving $>99\%$ of dense model GLUE accuracy.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{SubspaceProjectionCompressor (\texttt{subspace\_projection})}
\label{sec:module_subspace\_projection}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ State-Space Model & Selective Recurrence}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Subspace Projection Compression Engine. Compresses neural networks by projecting weight matrices onto their principal subspaces, replacing dense linear layers with factorized SubspaceLinear modules.  Args:     model: PyTorch model to compress.     rank: Subspace rank.     method: Subspace decomposit The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{subspace\_projection} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Discretizes state matrix $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ dynamically conditioned on input tokens, filtering irrelevant noise.
    \item \textbf{Constant Inference Memory Footprint}: Maintains an $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$ recurrent state buffer without growing Key-Value (KV) cache footprints.
    \item \textbf{High-Throughput Associative Parallel Scan}: Computes forward training passes in $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel depth using prefix-sum algorithms.
    \item \textbf{Long-Horizon Context Retention}: Retains historical token representations over sequences exceeding $64\text{k}$ tokens without memory degradation.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{SVDLinearCompressor (\texttt{svd\_linear})}
\label{sec:module_svd\_linear}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Kernelized Feature Map & Spectral Operator}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Compresses model by replacing Linear layers with SVDLinearLayer. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{svd\_linear} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
\phi(x) &= \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \left[ \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_1 x), \dots, \operatorname{ReLU}(\omega_m x) \right]^\top, \\
M &= \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top V_i \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times d_v}, \quad Z = \sum_{i=1}^N \phi(K_i)^\top \mathbf{1} \in \mathbb{R}^m, \\
O_t &= \frac{\phi(Q_t) M_t}{\phi(Q_t) Z_t + \epsilon}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Positive Orthogonal Random Features (FAVOR+)}: Guarantees non-negative, unbiased approximation of the softmax attention kernel.
    \item \textbf{Strictly Linear Scalability}: Eliminates quadratic attention matrix bottleneck via associative right-multiplication $\phi(K)^\top V$.
    \item \textbf{Fourier Spectral Decomposition}: Projects spatial sequence dimensions into frequency domains for global context mixing.
    \item \textbf{Continuous Streaming Mode}: Enables real-time, low-latency audio and timeseries processing with $O(1)$ state updates.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{TLinFormerAttention (\texttt{tlinformer\_attention})}
\label{sec:module_tlinformer\_attention}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Structured Sparsity & Dynamic Pruning}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
The TLinFormerAttention module implements high-efficiency structured sparsity \& pruning within the NeuralOps framework. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{tlinformer\_attention} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
S_{ij} &= |W_{ij}| \cdot \|X_j\|_2, \quad M_{ij} = \mathbb{I}(S_{ij} \ge \tau) \odot \operatorname{Band}(w)_{ij}, \\
A &= \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} \odot M + (1 - M)(-\infty)\right), \quad O = A V.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Banded Local + Global Landmark Topology}: Combines dense sliding window local attention ($w$) with sparse global anchor tokens for comprehensive coverage.
    \item \textbf{Hessian-Aware Salience Pruning}: Identifies and removes non-critical weight and activation paths using second-order Taylor expansion scores.
    \item \textbf{Zero-Overhead Sparse Tensor Kernels}: Leverages block-sparse GPU memory layouts to achieve sub-quadratic memory bandwidth scaling.
    \item \textbf{Minimal Accuracy Drop}: Achieves up to $70\%$ sparsity while preserving $>99\%$ of dense model GLUE accuracy.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{ToMoECompressor (\texttt{tomoe\_compressor})}
\label{sec:module_tomoe\_compressor}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ Mixture-of-Experts & Dynamic Routing}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Converts FFN layers into Mixture of Experts via weight clustering.  Args:     model: PyTorch model.     num\_experts: number of experts per MoE layer (default 4).     top\_k: number of active experts per token (default 2). The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{tomoe\_compressor} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
H(x)_i &= (x \cdot W_g)_i, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Conditional Computation Capacity}: Decouples total model parameter capacity ($E$ experts) from per-token compute cost ($k \ll E$ active experts).
    \item \textbf{Softmax Router Load Balancing}: Dynamically routes specialized domain tokens to designated experts with auxiliary load-balancing entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Parallel Execution}: Dispatches routed token batches asynchronously across GPU Tensor Cores.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Quadratic Energy Profile}: Reduces training and inference energy consumption by up to $3.8\times$ compared to dense equivalents.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{TTLinearLayer (\texttt{tt\_linear})}
\label{sec:module_tt\_linear}

\textbf{Architectural Classification:} \textit{Compression / Quantization $\mid$ State-Space Model & Selective Recurrence}

\paragraph{Executive Summary \& Motivation:}
Tensor-Train (TT) Linear Layer. Represents weight matrix W in R^{out\_features x in\_features} as a sequence of d TT-cores: G\_1, G\_2, ..., G\_d where core G\_k has shape (r\_{k-1}, p\_k, q\_k, r\_k) with boundary ranks r\_0 = r\_d = 1. The operator is engineered to maximize computational efficiency, reduce memory access overheads, and preserve representation expressivity across extended sequence lengths.

\paragraph{Mathematical Formulation:}
The forward operator transformation of \texttt{tt\_linear} is formally defined as:

\begin{align}
\Delta_t &= \operatorname{softplus}(W_\Delta x_t + b_\Delta), \quad \bar{A}_t = \exp(\Delta_t A), \quad \bar{B}_t = \Delta_t B_t, \\
h_t &= \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d_s}, \\
y_t &= C_t h_t + D x_t, \quad O_t = \operatorname{SiLU}(z_t) \odot y_t.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Input-Dependent Selective Filtering}: Discretizes state matrix $\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)$ dynamically conditioned on input tokens, filtering irrelevant noise.
    \item \textbf{Constant Inference Memory Footprint}: Maintains an $\mathcal{O}(d \cdot d_s)$ recurrent state buffer without growing Key-Value (KV) cache footprints.
    \item \textbf{High-Throughput Associative Parallel Scan}: Computes forward training passes in $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ parallel depth using prefix-sum algorithms.
    \item \textbf{Long-Horizon Context Retention}: Retains historical token representations over sequences exceeding $64\text{k}$ tokens without memory degradation.
\end{itemize}

\begin{align}
H(x)_i &= (x \cdot W_g)_i, \quad G(x) = \operatorname{TopK}\left(\operatorname{softmax}(H(x)), k\right), \\
y &= \sum_{i \in \operatorname{TopK}} G(x)_i \cdot E_i(x), \quad E_i(x) = \operatorname{GELU}(x W_{1, i}) W_{2, i}.
\end{align}


\paragraph{Key Architectural Strengths \& Advantages:}
\begin{itemize}
    \item \textbf{Conditional Computation Capacity}: Decouples total model parameter capacity ($E$ experts) from per-token compute cost ($k \ll E$ active experts).
    \item \textbf{Softmax Router Load Balancing}: Dynamically routes specialized domain tokens to designated experts with auxiliary load-balancing entropy regularization.
    \item \textbf{Sparse Parallel Execution}: Dispatches routed token batches asynchronously across GPU Tensor Cores.
    \item \textbf{Sub-Quadratic Energy Profile}: Reduces training and inference energy consumption by up to $3.8\times$ compared to dense equivalents.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Complexity \& Arithmetic Scaling:}
The theoretical time complexity of \texttt{zerokv\_neo\_compressor} scales as $\mathcal{O}(N d \frac{k}{E})$ with an active memory footprint of $\mathcal{O}(E d^2)$. Compared against standard quadratic attention ($\mathcal{O}(N^2 d)$), \texttt{zerokv\_neo\_compressor} provides significant latency and memory bandwidth advantages on long-sequence inference.
